about: The cleaning domain's truth mappings for claims about its state (kernel/speech.py truth(); VERIFY_HARDENING 13.1-13.3, 13.6; WP-D cleaning; the format of truth.json, whose keys this file never repeats). Cleaning owns soil (docs/domains/cleaning.md section 0: an entity's soil dict {kind: level 0..1} is the max over its faces, shadows and floor cells; a kind is clean below 0.05), cleaning products, waste streams and bin fill. states: clean / dirty read the highest soil level of the subject ($max:soil, the pseudo-field the kernel reads as the largest number of a dict field: until speech._field reads it the claim is unscored, never wrong); full is a bin, vacuum bin, product or caddy at 90 % of its fill (fill_level, recomputed from what it holds); soapy / rinsed read the soap left on a washed thing (cl_suds, rinsing clears it); sanitized reads the subject's highest contamination ($max:contamination). issues (any present condition that holds makes it true, all present and false make it false): a soil kind at 0.05 or more (dusty, crumbs, sticky, greasy, stained over the stain kinds, streaky, water_spots, fingerprints, mildew, rusty), finish harm in the damage dict (etched), a waste item in a stream it does not belong to (wrong_bin: stream_ok false), a bin past full (overfull), hair around a vacuum's brush roll (hair_wrapped), raw-meat or toilet germs carried onto a surface (cross_contaminated), fruit flies at a caddy. A floor's wetness follows its room's water film (state.sync_floor_wetness), so the kernel's wet / dry states read a mopped floor. acts: clean (I cleaned / will clean X) is lenient: one of the robot's cleaning verbs on the subject, or the end state for a commitment.
